speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the onset and progression of your gait and limb ataxia, and list any other significant symptoms you are experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of alcohol abuse, or do you have any family members with similar symptoms? I also need to know if you have experienced any headaches, vision changes, or difficulty swallowing.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent fever, stiff neck, or confusion, and are you currently taking any other medications that might affect your immune system or neurological function?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

text: The MRI findings are classic for PML, but the normal JC Virus Index is unexpected and requires clarification. Could you confirm if the JC Virus Index was an IgG antibody test or a PCR test for viral DNA in the blood or cerebrospinal fluid?

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings are highly specific for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy, a known complication of natalizumab therapy. The normal blood JC virus index does not rule out the disease, as the virus replicates in the brain, not the blood. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
